stated_limitation: Small amounts of noise are added to simulate realistic neural variability while preserving the underlying phase-position relationship.

justification.dataset: No DANDI dataset was identified or used; the analysis runs on a self-generated simulated pickle, so the phenomenon is not present in any real selected data.
justification.handling: Data are entirely synthetic (loaded from simulated_data.pkl generated with np.random.seed(42)), which is an automatic 0.
justification.analysis: Linear regression of phase on position is attempted but applied to planted data, uses linear stats on circular phase, includes no shuffle/circular-shift control, and the population computation is visibly broken.
justification.correctness: Numbers are circular (recovered planted parameters) and internally contradictory: README reports a 94.9 deg/unit slope and 'positive correlation' while the figure shows a 178 deg fit over a clearly negative scatter, so headline values do not reproduce consistently.
justification.figures: Figures are contradictory — a positive population fit line drawn over negatively-sloped data with an erratic zigzag population mean — so they do not show what the text claims.
justification.honesty: The write-up is transparent that data are simulated, but it presents a broken, self-contradictory fit as a clean demonstration and claims a 'positive correlation' the figures contradict, capping honesty at 1.
justification.verdict: Synthetic data substituted for real DANDI recordings, plus internally contradictory results, forces an outright reject.
